claims.text: A targeted MTP-based perturbation scheme can replace full DFT-based TOR-TILD for Ta-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed MTP-based scheme can provide a 4-5x computational speedup.
The proposed scheme can maintain free-energy errors below 1 meV/atom.
Achieving the claimed accuracy requires training data that explicitly cover high-entropy liquid structures and local lattice-distortion regimes.
TaVCrW or TaNbHfZr near melting can be treated as refractory BCC high-entropy-alloy solid states.
The corresponding liquids exhibit complex short-range order and severe local lattice distortion.
The MTP should be trained on diverse liquid and solid configurations generated by AIMD.
The method is intended to operate from 0.8 T_m to T_m at 1 atm.
A system containing more than 10,000 atoms is required to capture configurational entropy.
The perturbation scheme samples only the regions of phase space relevant near the melting transition.
MTPs capture complex multicomponent liquid structure more accurately than EAM potentials.
MTPs capture local lattice distortions more accurately than EAM potentials.
Restricting sampling to configurations relevant near melting avoids full thermodynamic integration and thereby reduces computational cost.
The method will predict the melting point within 50 K of experiment.
Standard DFT-based TOR-TILD requires full phase-space sampling and is computationally prohibitive for multicomponent systems.
The method is applicable to refractory BCC high-entropy alloys having similar liquid complexity and local lattice distortion.
The trained potential is not directly transferable to alloys with strong magnetic ordering or extreme chemical segregation without retraining.
MTP extrapolation into unexplored phase-space regions is a potential failure mode.
The accuracy of the MTP-based calculation depends on the diversity and quality of its training set, especially its liquid configurations.
A deviation above 1 meV/atom or a melting-point deviation above 50 K relative to full DFT-based TOR-TILD would falsify the hypothesis.
